life? Are we prepared to take seriously the thought of
eternity, and to engage in our activities in the light of
eternity, to place them under the judgment of eternity?
Yes, do we know any higher life? Do we know anything
of the future, of the transcendent? If we are honest we must
admit that we have no direct experience of it, and we know
nothing about it. What we do know, and what we have
immediate experience of, is ever and only our life up to the
present; our lite here below, the lite of our earthly destiny,
the life of our plans and projects. But to reckon with eternity
means just this: to view our familiar life as a provisional,
unfulfilled and unfulfillable life, and to live it in preparation
for a future fulfilled and true life which God wills to bestow
on us. If we were to try to picture the future to ourselves, we
should only fill it out with the images suggested by our
wishes and dreams. Now it is just these fantasies which we are
to surrender. To be ready for God's future means to walk
trustfully into the darkness, ready for the purposes which
God in His wisdom designs us to fulfil.
This future which flows from God does not however meet
us only at the end of our days, but he who listens to the
divine call may now already and ever afresh experience the
way in which God makes him purer and stronger, more
serene and cheerful, how God fulfils the prayer: "Make me
pure, tender-hearted, detached from the things of sense,
calm and gentle, poised in the peace which passes under-
standing!" The man who has cultivated this preparedness
for God's call in the course of his earthly life will also find
himself prepared for the final call of God summoning him
out of this our familiar world into the darkness of the un-
known. The fact that this final summons will at some time or
other be sounded for us, forms the greatest disturbance of
all. How few men there are for whom this last call of God is
not the most unwelcome of their whole experience! For
how few does it come at the right time! And who would not,
if only he could, beg for postponement, so that he might put
